name: Electro-osmotic glaucoma drain
subtitle: an eye drain with no moving parts

effects.effect: a voltage across a wet porous material makes the liquid flow

effect: a voltage across a wet porous material makes the liquid flow
how: Glaucoma blinds slowly as fluid pressure builds inside the eye; drops get forgotten, and drain implants either drain too little or so much the eye goes soft. A grain-sized plug of porous glass sits in the eye wall with an electrode on each face: a small voltage makes the eye's fluid flow through its pores (electro-osmosis), so a chip reading a pressure sensor drains exactly enough to hold pressure steady.
obstacle: Running for decades inside the eye without the electrodes corroding or making gas bubbles.
why: Glaucoma is a leading cause of blindness; a drain that can speed up or stop fixes both failure modes.
real: US patent 8603024 describes a glaucoma drainage device whose valve is governed by an electro-osmotic membrane between electrodes; other patents cover electrolysis/electrocapillary pumps with IOP sensors, but no working demonstration found.
